appraisal_events.evidence: j'entendis Bloch dire en parlant de lui-même : « ... c'était Bloch »... la même phrase dans la bouche de bien d'autres jeunes gens qui ne la connaissaient pas et qui remplaçaient seulement Bloch par leur propre nom
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator quotes Bloch's grandiose self-praise, then reveals that other vain young men used the identical formula substituting only their own name, ironically exposing it as a hollow, interchangeable cliché rather than genuine distinction.

appraisal_events.evidence: il avait dans son ménage l'habitude d'être brutal avec elle... il s'arrêta net et lança sur la duchesse un regard qui embarrassa tout le monde
appraisal_events.explanation: The duke habitually dominates his wife and cuts off her interruption with a glare that visibly embarrasses the company, staging her as subordinate within the couple.

appraisal_events.evidence: si un des nôtres était refusé au Jockey, et surtout Saint-Loup dont le père y a été pendant dix ans président, ce serait un comble... Je ne peux pas leur donner tort... quand on s'appelle le marquis de Saint-Loup, on n'est pas dreyfusard
appraisal_events.explanation: The duke invokes Saint-Loup's father's prestigious tenure to argue his exclusion from the Jockey Club would be unthinkable, while simultaneously endorsing the club's shock at his Dreyfusism as incongruous with his aristocratic name.

status_effects.explanation: Bloch's self-praise is deflated by the narrator's ironic exposure of it as a common, interchangeable formula, undercutting its sincerity.
She is silenced and dominated by her husband's habitual brutality in front of company.

His Dreyfusism is framed as incongruous with his class name and tacitly endorsed as shocking by the duke, even as his father's prestige is invoked to argue against his exclusion, yielding a net mild negative local positioning.

ambiguities: The duke's remarks on Saint-Loup are genuinely mixed — protective of his family prestige against Jockey Club exclusion, yet also validating the club's shock at his Dreyfusism — so the net local effect on Saint-Loup is read conservatively as mildly negative rather than sharply determined.
